4. Evidence by requirement / acceptance criterion
AC: **Core Functionality** – Support `@supports story-path REQ-ID1 REQ-ID2 ...` format - Implementation: - `src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts` detects `@supports` in comments and delegates to helpers: - Uses a regex like `/@supports\b/` to detect the tag. - Extracts the value after `@supports` and passes it to `validateImplementsAnnotation`. - `src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts`: - `MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS = 2` ensures at least ` `. - `parseImplementsTokens` splits the value into `{ storyPath, reqIds }`, where `storyPath` is the first token and `reqIds` are the remaining tokens. - Tests (all passing): - `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts`: - `"[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid single @supports with one story and one requirement (default patterns)"` - `"[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid multiple @supports lines with different stories and requirements"`
AC / REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE: **Parse @supports** - The above implementation and tests confirm correct parsing of `@supports` into story path and one or more requirement IDs.
AC: **Validation** – Validate each requirement exists in its specified story file - Implementation: - `src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts` and `src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts`: - `parseImplementsLine(line: string)` parses a full `@supports` line into `{ storyPath, reqIds }`. - `validateImplementsLine` calls `resolveStoryAndRequirements` to resolve the path and load all requirement IDs from that story file into a `Set`. - For each `reqId` in `reqIds`, it calls `checkRequirementExists`, which reports `messageId: 'reqMissing'` when the ID is not present. - Tests (all passing) from `tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts`: - Valid cases: - `"[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single supports line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)"` - `"[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story supports with shared requirement IDs (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)"` - Invalid case: - `"[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing supports requirement in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)"` – asserts `reqMissing` is reported when a requirement ID is absent from the specified story.
AC / REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE: **Validate each requirement** – satisfied by the above.
AC: **Backward Compatibility** – Existing `@story` + `@req` continue working unchanged (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT) - Implementation: - `valid-annotation-format` continues to support the legacy `@story` and `@req` paths as before; `@supports` behavior is additive and does not alter legacy parsing functions. - `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` rules detect `@supports` *in addition* to the existing `@story` and `@req` markers, without changing their original semantics. - Tests (all passing): - `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` still contains extensive tests for legacy `@story` and `@req` behavior that are unchanged and passing. - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts`: - Includes a BACKCOMPAT invalid test: `"[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED][BACKCOMPAT] missing @story annotation on function with no @supports"` – still errors exactly as before. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`: - Multiple tests verify legacy `@req` behavior, including both valid and invalid scenarios; all pass, showing no regression.
AC: **Mixed Usage** – Support both annotation styles in the same codebase/file (REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT) - Implementation: - `valid-annotation-format` processes comments line-by-line and supports seeing `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` tags in the same block without conflict. - `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` detect any of these tags as satisfying their respective requirements; they do not assume mutual exclusivity. - Tests: - `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts`: - `"[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment"` – verifies that a single comment containing all three tags is accepted and properly validated.
AC: **Error Messages** – Include story path when validation fails (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT) - Implementation: - In `src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts`: - Message definition: `reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'"`. - `checkRequirementExists` (helper) populates `data` with both `reqId` and `storyPath`. - Tests: - `tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts` invalid `@supports` cases assert that `reqMissing` is emitted with the correct `storyPath` and `reqId` data. - The verbose Jest output includes these tests under `Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)`, all passing.
AC: **Requirement Scoping** – IDs only need to be unique within their story file (REQ-SCOPED-IDS) - Implementation: - `loadAndCacheRequirements(storyPath, cache)` reads each story file and stores a separate `Set` of requirement IDs per resolved story path. - Validation uses the `Set` corresponding to the specific story path, meaning the same REQ ID can appear in multiple files without conflict. - Tests: - Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md` and `tests/fixtures/story_multi_b.md` each define `REQ-SHARED-ID` and a file-specific ID. - `tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts` valid cases: - One test validates `@supports tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID REQ-ONLY-A`. - Another validates two `@supports` lines, one per story fixture, each referencing `REQ-SHARED-ID` and its own unique ID. - These passing tests confirm requirement IDs are scoped per story file and can be reused across different stories.
AC / REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION: **Validate @supports line format** - Implementation: - `src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts`: - Ensures at least story path + one REQ ID (`MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS`). - Validates story path against `storyPattern` and provides specific error messages when invalid. - Validates each requirement ID against `reqPattern` and reports `invalidReqFormat` errors when mismatched. - `src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts` defines `invalidImplementsFormat` and other messages used when format checks fail. - Tests (all passing): `tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` includes: - `"[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with no value is invalid"`. - `"[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with only story path and no requirement IDs is invalid"`. - `"[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid story path format"`. - `"[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid requirement ID format"` and `"... where one is invalid"`.
REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS: `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` accept @supports - Implementation: - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts`: - Functions like `commentContainsStory`, `linesBeforeHasStory`, `parentChainHasStory`, and `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` treat both `"@story"` and `"@supports"` as satisfying markers. - `src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts`: - Functions `commentContainsReq`, `linesBeforeHasReq`, `parentChainHasReq`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq`, and `hasReqInJsdocOrComments` treat both `"@req"` and `"@supports"` as valid requirement markers. - Tests (all passing): - `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts`: - Includes a valid case where only `@supports` is present; the rule accepts it as satisfying the story annotation requirement. - `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`: - Includes a valid case where only `@supports` provides the requirement IDs; the rule accepts it as satisfying the requirement annotation requirement.
AC: **Quality Standards** – ESLint rule best practices - All involved rules (`valid-annotation-format`, `valid-req-reference`, `require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`) follow ESLint best practices: - Each exports `meta` with `docs` and `schema`. - Behavior is broken into small, focused helper modules. - RuleTester-based tests cover valid and invalid cases, including multi-story and mixed-annotation scenarios. - The full test suite passes, providing strong regression protection.
AC: **Documentation** – Examples and migration guidance - Story file `docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md` itself documents: - New `@supports` annotation format with concrete examples. - Legacy `@story` + `@req` format. - Mixed-usage examples combining both. - Parsing and validation logic, including expected error messages. - ADR alignment: - `docs/decisions/011-rename-implements-to-supports-annotation.accepted.md` formalizes the rename from `@implements` to `@supports` and clarifies that `@supports` is the canonical multi-story annotation, matching this story’s intent.
5. Regression / backward-compatibility check via tests - Multiple suites that validate behavior from earlier stories (001.0, 002.0, 003.0, 005.0, 006.0, 010.0) all pass in the current run, demonstrating that adding `@supports` did not break existing functionality.
